chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: Saving to buy the family property near Normandie
summary: Working on streetcar lines, Spikes and his mother saved about a thousand dollars and bought land on Thirty-Fifth near Normandie in 1907.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: About two years, I think. Then, as I told you, after that I went on the railroad after that. I was a little bigger, and then my brother came home, you know. The money that I made on the railroad and things--see, I worked on there about a year, year-and-a-half, I think, building that railroad--then we built another railroad from downtown that went up to...do you know where California Street is?

It's up a northwest...uh, north of First Street. Well, anyway, there's a California Street up there, and we built a railroad--streetcar--a way out California Street, so I worked on that awhile, and I worked about two years and uh, between my mother and I, we saved up about, maybe a thousand dollars or so, and we bought some property on Thirty-Fifth and...on Thirty-Fifth...near Normandie. I still got it. That was 1907. I still got the property there. So I'm keepin' it because my mother died there, and my father died there, and my sister died there, my brother died there, so I don't know, I just...I've never tried to sell it.
